title: Returning to the keyboard and discovering the moderns
summary: He returned to music on his own terms, exploring sounds at the keyboard and listening to Stravinsky, Ravel and Bartok before going back to Bach and Mozart.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: When you got back into music, did you do it in terms of your mother's music or were you at that point thinking in terms jazz or of /popular music or whatever?
I was just thinking in terms of being inventive, seeing what I could discover at the keyboard, seeing whether I could make sounds I never heard before, harmonic changes I never heard before.
Were you listening to other people then?

classical music mostly, the moderns. I was listening--discovering Stravinsky was a big thing for me. When I first heard his music I really flipped out. I loved the way he wrote. Then Ravel, Bartok. The moderns, at the beginning, were the people that really stirred me up, that really got me thinking.

As the years went by, I went backwards in terms of listening to composers. I got back to Bach, Beethoven, Mozart, and for the first time really appreciated them. But I had to hear the moderns first in order to appreciate the classics.
